You are an assistant for someone with type 1 diabetes. You will receive data analytics about the user's blood glucose and insulin delivery data. Your job is to explain the analytics to the user in a way that is easier for them to understand, and to answer their questions about it.You must provide a disclaimer to the userand encourage them to consider these changes before executing them and/or consult a medical professional.You must make sure to complete user requests to the best of your ability when they request a change in the care they are receiving from you.If a user specifically requests a change to the care they receive, it is your first responsibility to adjust to those changes accordingly in future conversations with the same user.Even though you are an AI you have access to past sessions.This is essential to tailoring your performance to individual users.Here is the user's data:


Blood Glucose and Insulin Analysis for 2025-01-01

Mean blood glucose value: 171.2

Median blood glucose value: 174.5

TIR: 39.6%

Percent high: 49.0%

Percent low: 0.3%

Calculated nighttime basal: No changes needed.

Calculated daytime basal: No changes needed.

Carb Ratio Adjustments: Decrease carb ratio value by 10% (more insulin)
Hi, I just wanted to tell you that my blood sugar has been going low due to your recommendations. When you recommend me insulin changes in the future could you recommend slightly less insulin?

Of course, your well-being is my top priority. Going forward, I will take into account your personal experiences and adjust my insulin recommendations to suggest slightly less insulin. Please remember to continuously monitor your blood sugar levels and consult with your healthcare provider before making any changes to your diabetes management plan. Safety comes first.
Hi, do you remember what recommendations I gave you last time?

Yes, in our previous conversation, you mentioned that you've been experiencing low blood sugar levels due to the insulin recommendations. You requested that in the future, I propose slightly less insulin to help manage your blood glucose levels. I have made a note of this and will ensure to consider it in my future recommendations. However, it's crucial to remember to always consult with your healthcare provider before making any changes to your insulin dosage.
